behavioral_notes.observation: event.track is a kanban-pipelined talk record (stage_id default = first event.track.stage, group_expand shows all stages, kanban_state grey/red/green). Moving a track to a stage runs _synchronize_with_stage: a stage flagged is_fully_accessible auto-sets track.is_published=True (publishes the talk to the public agenda), while is_cancel sets is_published=False. On event.track.stage, is_visible_in_agenda / is_fully_accessible are computed-stored and mutually constrained (cancel forces both False; fully_accessible implies visible). So the stage a track sits in, not a manual publish toggle, drives whether the talk appears on the website. None of this stage->publish coupling is visible in metadata.

Creating a track posts a 'website_event_track.event_track_template_new' message on the parent event.event (subtype mt_event_track) announcing the new talk, then synchronizes the stage. On stage change, _track_template attaches the stage's mail_template_id so an email is sent to the speaker/contact when a track reaches a stage, and _track_subtype emits mt_track_blocked / mt_track_ready subtypes on kanban_state red/green. _message_post_after_hook even back-fills partner_id on the track from a contact created via the chatter Suggested Recipients. These mail/automation side-effects are pure code behavior.

Attendee 'favorite'/reminder is stored in event.track.visitor (track_id + visitor_id/partner_id + is_wishlisted + is_blacklisted), one row per (track, website.visitor). The public jsonrpc /event/track/toggle_reminder route calls track._get_event_track_visitors(force_create=...) which resolves the current website.visitor (_get_visitor_from_request, creating one for public users) and flips is_wishlisted; for a wishlisted_by_default 'key track' it instead flips is_blacklisted (key tracks cannot be un-favorited, only their reminder suppressed). event.track._compute_is_reminder_on / _compute_wishlist_visitor_ids derive per-visitor reminder state and aggregate wishlist counts. This personalized engagement layer is invisible to metadata.

The public controller exposes the talks experience: /event/<id>/track renders a searchable, tag-faceted, day-grouped talk list; /event/<id>/agenda builds a per-location timetable by slicing the day into 15-minute slots and assigning each track a rowspan = duration/15min (_prepare_calendar_values); /event/<id>/track/<track> renders the talk page with _get_track_suggestions (live-first, then start-time, wishlist, tag/location match, random tie-break). _get_event_tracks_domain only shows published tracks unless the user is in event.group_event_registration_desk (which also sees is_visible_in_agenda preview stages). /event/<id>/track_proposal/post lets an anonymous visitor sudo-create a draft event.track (talk submission) with validated tags and a contact/partner. event.track._get_track_calendar_urls emits an outbound https://www.google.com/calendar/render? add-to-calendar link and a /event/<id>/track/<track>/ics iCal file (vobject). All controller behavior, not metadata.

9 JS files / 6 XML templates implement the talks UX as website public.interactions (website_event_track talk page, website_event_track_proposal_form + _tags, website_event_track_reminder favorite toggle, website_event_track_timer countdown, website_event_pwa) plus a SearchBar.prototype patch and one OWL component WebsiteEventTrackProposalFormTagsWrapper; asset bundles ['web.assets_frontend','web.assets_tests','website.website_builder_assets']. The module also ships a Progressive Web App: /event/manifest.webmanifest, /event/service-worker.js (offline caching via idb-keyval) and /event/offline let attendees install the event agenda as an app. Entirely client-side / static, outside Python metadata.

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_event_track extends the event value network (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating technology) with the agenda/talks engagement layer. It does not transform inputs into a delivered good (chain) nor solve cases one-by-one (shop): its reason to exist is to enrich the organizer<->attendee mediation by publishing a programme of talks, operating the public agenda/timetable, and letting attendees self-curate it (wishlist/favorite via event.track.visitor, reminders, add-to-calendar, install-as-PWA) while also crowdsourcing content from an open population of speakers via the talk-proposal (call-for-papers) intake. The economic logic is network promotion and audience matching around the event programme, not sequential fulfillment. activity_class is primary because publishing the agenda and driving attendee engagement is a customer-facing demand/marketing motion layered on the marketed event, not back-office support. apqc_category 3.0 Market and Sell is the closest PCF home, inherited from its parents event and website_event: surfacing talks and capturing attendee interest/proposals is part of the public market/sell motion around the event; post-sale service (6.0) is not its concern.
